schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The post-build gate: python SIEVES that judge orient's measurements and red a build whose component fails one. Founding sieves (cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py): `charter_on_disk` — code with no intention+why.json; `proofs_exist` — code with zero proofs (Law 8); `silent_device` — a BaseDevice subclass that never calls emit() outside proofs (the MAP.md:434 claim, enforced); `state_is_projection` — state.json must equal project(history.json), the drift check half of the compiled-view IOU. `inspect(component=...)` gates one build; `inspect()` is the whole-repo sweep. CLI exits 0 clean / 1 findings — gate-able by anything that reads an exit code. The verdict is always HARDWARE (ruling 2026-07-28, held-nexi-everywhere — reworded from 'inference-free by construction'): no deepen seam exists at fire-time; a gate that consults an oracle is not a gate. Inference may serve the LEARNING of sieves, but a learning lands here only by installation — evidence-provenanced, ratified, versioned — never mid-fire; a verdict's replayability (same input + same registry revision = same verdict) is what lets it be permanent in a record of truth (Law 7). SECOND SEAT AT THE SAME DOOR (2026-07-29, ticket buildme-rides-the-chart): the ENTRY GATE — buildme_rides_the_chart, crossing-jurisdiction, deliberately NOT in SIEVES (the promotion sweep has no crossing context and would retro-red pre-chain components) — called from the emit chokepoint's forward-into-BUILDME branch: a cast ticket may not begin building unless a berthed validate packet claims it. Promotion judges a build AGAINST its chart; entry requires the chart to EXIST. /chart is physics now, not sail-prose. THIRD SEAT, THE LOOP CLOSES (2026-07-29, ticket proved-answers-the-chart): the EXIT GATE — proved_answers_the_chart, same crossing-jurisdiction, same NOT-in-SIEVES reason — called from the emit chokepoint's forward-into-PROVED branch: a claimed cast ticket may not close unless a verdict artifact (cairn/devices/builder/machines/verdict/verdict.py, the ONE tree-free validator shared with the deposit face) answers every criterion of the claiming validate berth with a passing run verdict and dispositions every hypothesis confirmed-or-killed. UNCLAIMED IS GREEN — the inversion of the entry check (entry demands a chart exists; exit judges only the chart that claims) — and a cast-but-unclaimed crossing journals gated-and-clean, never silently ungated. Entry gates the door, promotion judges the middle, exit measures the close: done by instrument at every mouth of the one chokepoint. SINCE 2026-08-06 THE SIEVES ARE A NEST: they are shaken ONCE, coarse band first, and what comes out is a GRADATION — a score per sieve per component — rather than a pass/fail. Each sieve's BAND IS DERIVED from what its own body reaches (import_sieve.reach_of over this module's source), never authored: in-hand / local-disk / correlated-local / off-box. SINCE 2026-08-07 the assembly and the shake themselves ride the general berth (`cairn/tools/base/nest.py`, ruling 2026-08-07-the-nest-is-block-general) — this inspector is TENANT #1: it brings the firing closure and the derived reaches; the ordering, the gradation and the min() roll-up are the general side's. A finding carries the datum (`evidence`, under the name it has always had) AND a `score` — the datum read against the requirement.
why: Akien, 2026-07-27, verbatim: 'the next thing is a post build inspector (also in python with SIEVES) that can catch these kinds of things. we find a new thing, we add a new sieve. can also be a seperate, command line only inference free operation to run it on the whole repo once built. we should only ever have to do that once.' The deeper why is his older observation that CC does not add logging (and its kin) until told — 'i have been resigned to the fact that we wouldn't have such logging until some lever presented itself... and a post build inspector is just the thing.' The lever is Law 4: a discipline in CC's habit is policy; a sieve at the build gate is physics. 'Only once' holds by construction — the sweep brings the existing tree to the gate one time, then every build passes through the inspector, so wanting a second sweep is itself a finding (a build bypassed the gate). WHY A NEST RATHER THAN A LIST (ruling 2026-08-06-a-stack-of-sieves-is-a-nest, ticket the-questions-are-the-sieve): a flat registry has no answer to 'which check should have run first', and hand-numbering the checks would make inserting one a WRITE TO ITS NEIGHBOURS (Law 6). Deriving the band from the sieve's own reach makes the ordering a characteristic of the KIND OF THING the check does rather than of where it is installed — Akien: 'greater reusability' — and it cannot go stale, because a sieve that starts reaching further drops a band by itself at the next derivation. A hand-labeled nest would keep it near the top and nobody would notice.
invoke: import: `from cairn.machines.build_inspector import inspector`. Prove: `python3 cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/test_inspector.py`. Gate one component: `python3 -m cairn.machines.build_inspector.inspector <component>`. The sweep: no argument.

Two consumers, and both already exist. (1) THE MACHINE — cairn/tools/base/transitions.py, the emit chokepoint: it reads `findings` (sieve, finding, why_it_matters, evidence) and `clean`, and refuses the forward crossing out of PROVEME before anything is written (BuildGateRed). This is the consumer that makes the gate physics rather than a report. (2) AKIEN — the disposition of a finding on a component he owns is his (see `owner`), and the finding's text is written to be read by him at that gate. WHAT HAS NO CONSUMER YET: the `gradation` / `component_scores` / per-finding `score` added 2026-08-06 are read by nothing outside this module and its proofs (measured corpus-wide at birth, re-measured at the lift). By Akien's definition they are therefore NOT FINDINGS YET — an emission looking for something to operate on. Emitted at the general level, watched for a reader — never dressed as a feature.

(i) A CHECK IS WORTH ITS MESH — ruling 2026-08-05-a-check-is-worth-its-mesh, and it is the rule that makes a gate's certificate mean anything. Akien: 'it's not ever proof of file path for our inspections teams: it's AT LEAST proof of a not empty file. if it's supposed to be json, then it's proof of a valid json file... if that field has to have a range, then that's what the sieve looks for.' So THE CHECK MUST BE AS STRONG AS THE CLAIM IT CERTIFIES, and existence is never the check. The ladder is a MESH GRADING, coarse to fine: exists and non-empty -> parses as its declared format -> carries its declared field -> that field is in its declared range. AND THE ONE THAT LIES QUIETLY: a SAMPLED check ('the top x% sure looks like valid JSON') must RECORD ITS SAMPLE, because 'valid at 5%' and 'valid' are different claims and the weaker one otherwise reads as the stronger forever after (Law 3, Law 7). This is Law 8 turned from an entry condition into a standing property: a hollow build cannot pass, AND a hollow check cannot certify. Load-bearing under ruling 2026-08-05-gates-issue-clearances, where a clearance is worth exactly what its gate's mesh caught and no more.

(j) THE WORD BECOMES SIEVE — ruling 2026-08-05-sieves-become-sieves, NOT YET APPLIED and deliberately not applied tonight. Every inspector, one word, because the implementations must fork (edge (g) on diagnostic_inspector) and the vocabulary is the only thing left holding them as one idea. What the word buys beyond de-overloading 'sieve': MESH — 'which mesh does this one run' is a question with an answer, where 'sieve strength' is not, and edge (i)'s ladder IS a mesh grading. Akien's reason, and it is the design's own: 'someone, artificial intelligence or animal intelligence or even akien intelligence all have their lives made simpler by carrying the same model.' TIMING IS PART OF THE RULING: before or after nothing-rides-loose adds working_tree_clean, NEVER DURING — a rename mid-build is how a proof ends up pinning a name that no longer exists. Footprint measured 2026-08-05: 223 occurrences over 40 files, most of them generic Python filtering that stays 'sieve'; the concept-sense is concentrated here, in the proofs, and in this charter.

(nest-a) THE DOMAIN CAME BACK FLATTER THAN THE METAPHOR, and the flatness is the finding. Measured 2026-08-06 over the 18 live sieves: in-hand 3, local-disk 2, correlated-local 13, off-box 0. So fine-grained ordering buys almost nothing here today. The off-box band being empty is a MEASUREMENT, not a rule — a band SEQUENCES, it never FORBIDS, and a distant sieve is expected (two hosts already; four laptops once ran this system overnight against local models).

(nest-b) NOT-APPLICABLE HAS NOTHING TO SUPPRESS YET, and this was measured rather than assumed. The ticket anticipated that a coarse catch would make finer sieves not-applicable, and named the charterless component as the payoff — 'no charter, and you still get thirteen findings about its chart packets'. FALSE, measured 2026-08-06: the thirteen chart judges hang off _component_tickets(), which reads history.json and returns an empty set when it is absent, so a charterless component already emits nothing from them. The live sweep is 1 finding over 24 components. The absence rule is therefore built into the report's SHAPE (a sieve that did not run is absent from the gradation, never scored 0.0 — Akien refused a third value) and no suppression is wired, because no measured case wants it. Wire it when a real one appears, not before.

(nest-c) THE ROLL-UP IS min(), NOT mean(). One zero sinks the component. Averaging would let a component buy past a real catch with a pile of passes, which defeats the point that a score is relative to the REQUIREMENT and not to the other sieves.
